title: Bitcoin adoption trends and market analysis for February 202
content:
TL;DR: Bitcoin's network, as of February 05, 2026, remains operationally robust at block 935,122, processing transactions with a significant hashrate of 916.44 EH/s. With an important difficulty adjustment just 302 blocks away, transactors must understand how the protocol's self-regulating mechanics ensure censorship resistance and monetary sovereignty, even as hashrate recalibrates from recent peaks. This ongoing demonstration of Proof-of-Work reinforces Bitcoin's position as the hardest money, demanding vigilance and informed action from its users.

The Report

Good morning, transactors. It's February 05, 2026, 13:42 UTC, and the Bitcoin network continues its relentless march forward, demonstrating its unparalleled resilience and self-correcting nature. At a current block height of 935,122, the chain is operational and processing value transfers globally, 24/7, without interruption. The computational power securing this network stands at a formidable 916.44 Exahashes per second (EH/s). While this figure represents an immense commitment of energy and hardware, it is important to note that it sits slightly below the approximate 977 EH/s observed just weeks prior on January 23, 2026, and remains below the November 2025 peak difficulty of 155.9 Terahashes (T).

This slight recalibration in hashrate is a natural part of Bitcoin's dynamic ecosystem, reflecting shifts in mining profitability, energy costs, and hardware efficiency across different regions. It underscores the competitive yet decentralized nature of the mining industry.
